common_name: Zucchini Elite (AAS-Winning Compact Dark-Green Hybrid Zucchini)

planting.note: Direct sow after all frost danger has passed and soil has warmed to at least 70°F; a compact, semi-bush habit suits smaller beds better than sprawling vine-type squash.

directions: Direct sow after all frost danger has passed and soil has warmed, spacing plants about 30 inches apart in full sun. Elite is an All-America Selections-winning hybrid valued for uniform, glossy dark-green fruit, strong yields, and improved tolerance to common summer squash viruses. Its tidy, semi-compact bush habit performs well in raised beds and smaller gardens where sprawling squash would be impractical. Harvest fruit at 6-7 inches for the sweetest flavor and most tender skin, checking plants every day or two during peak production.

common_name: Dunja Zucchini (Organic Multi-Virus-Resistant Green Summer Squash)

planting.note: Sow directly in warm soil about 1-2 weeks after the last spring frost, or start indoors slightly earlier for a head start in short-season regions.

directions: Sow seeds directly in warm soil 1-2 weeks after the last spring frost, or start indoors 2-3 weeks early for short-season climates. Dunja was bred specifically for organic growers and shows strong resistance to zucchini yellow mosaic virus, watermelon mosaic virus, and papaya ringspot virus, making it dependable where aphid-transmitted viruses commonly cut a squash planting short. The medium-green, cylindrical fruit forms on an open, easy-to-harvest plant; picking regularly at 6-8 inches keeps vigorous plants producing all season.

planting.note: Because fruit sets without pollination, seed can go in slightly earlier than standard zucchini and grow well under row cover or in a high tunnel.

directions: Because Partenon sets fruit without pollination, it can be sown a bit earlier than standard zucchini and grown successfully under row cover or in a high tunnel where pollinator activity is limited. Direct sow or transplant into warm, fertile soil in full sun, spacing plants about 30 inches apart. The dark-green, cylindrical fruit is exceptionally uniform, making Partenon a favorite among market growers who need consistent size and shape for bunching. Harvest young at 6-8 inches, since parthenocarpic zucchini can size up quickly once fruit set begins.

common_name: Yellowfin Zucchini (Bright Yellow Straight-Fruited Hybrid Squash)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger passes, in warm, fertile soil in full sun; harvest young for the mildest flavor and most tender skin.

directions: Direct sow after the danger of frost has passed, in full sun and fertile, well-drained soil, spacing plants about 30 inches apart. Yellowfin produces glossy, bright golden-yellow, straight cylindrical fruit on a compact, open bush plant, offering a color and shape alternative to more common golden zucchini types. Pick regularly at 6-7 inches long, since yellow-skinned summer squash can develop a tougher skin if left to oversize. The bright color makes Yellowfin easy to spot at harvest time and an attractive addition to mixed squash displays.

common_name: Benning's Green Tint Scallop Squash (Pale Silvery-Green Heirloom Pattypan)

planting.note: Direct sow once soil has warmed in spring; pick the scalloped fruit young and small for the finest-grained, most tender texture.

directions: Direct sow after soil has warmed in spring, spacing plants about 3 feet apart in full sun; this early-20th-century heirloom produces flattened, scalloped fruit in a pale, silvery-green that sets it apart from the more common yellow and white pattypan types. It was popular in home gardens well before many modern hybrid scallop squash were developed, valued for its fine-grained, nutty flavor when picked young. Harvest the scallop-shaped fruit at 3-4 inches across for the best texture, since older fruit becomes seedy and less tender.

common_name: Y-Star Squash (Golden Yellow Star-Shaped Heirloom Pattypan)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; harvest small for the sweetest flavor, or let a few fruit mature fully for seed saving.

directions: Direct sow after last frost in full sun, spacing plants about 3 feet apart in fertile, well-drained soil. Y-Star is an heirloom pattypan type distinguished by its pointed, star-like scalloped edges and rich golden-yellow color, giving it a more angular silhouette than the rounded scallop shape of other pattypan squash. Harvest small, at about 2-3 inches across, for the sweetest flavor and most tender skin; larger fruit can be left to mature for seed saving or ornamental use.

common_name: Green Meat Radish (Green-Skinned, Green-Fleshed Asian Radish)

planting.note: Sow in early spring or, for the best size and flavor, as a late-summer crop timed to mature in cool fall weather, similar to daikon.

directions: Direct sow about half an inch deep in loose, well-worked soil, thinning seedlings to 4-6 inches apart; because the roots grow larger than a typical spring radish, deep, stone-free soil helps them develop a smooth, well-formed shape. Green Meat is prized in Chinese cuisine for its bright green skin and vivid green-and-white interior flesh, a striking contrast to the familiar red-skinned, white-fleshed Western radishes. It has a milder, sweeter flavor than most spring radishes and holds its crisp texture well, making it good raw in salads or lightly cooked. For the best size and flavor it is often grown as a late-summer to fall crop like daikon, though early spring sowing also works.
